transcript: These powders look alike. A sensor asks what they are made of. On September 17th, Sciware announced its new US headquarters in Austin. Its planned lab is meant to help robotics teams test what material sensing could add. The sensor reads how a sample absorbs light. The different responses make a spectral signature. Sciware says its contact demonstration distinguishes sugar from flour. The company also describes teaching the system to recognize an unknown sample. For a machine deciding what to handle or sort, that missing knowledge matters. The Austin invitation is to test a real application. A promising signal still has to earn the next move.
